page: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is a dedicated CPU virtual server powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This hardware configuration is bundled with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2692.67, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 13.84 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks show limitations, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is weak, measuring 296.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 36.09 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 27.85 GB/sec.

The server demonstrates average capabilities in text processing, Geekbench ray tracing, and image processing. It exhibits weak performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Large language model inference is highly constrained, with medium 7B model prompt processing rated as poor. Qualitatively, the dedicated CPU allocation provides stable execution for single-threaded tasks, but the resource density and memory bandwidth limitations make it less suitable for highly parallelized compilation or high-throughput databases. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose computing, single-threaded processing tasks, and lightweight text or image processing.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx23 is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 4 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. While single-core performance is strong—evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2692.67 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression—multi-core and memory read bandwidth benchmarks generally fall into the bottom 25%. The instance lacks GPU acceleration and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It delivers average performance in text, image, and ray tracing workloads, but struggles with database operations, Redis SET throughput, and multi-core software compilation. This profile makes the ccx23 best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded processing, and lightweight applications that benefit from dedicated CPU resources without requiring high multi-threaded throughput or intensive memory bandwidth.
